root.name: Richter-Veresov Attack: Malich Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nc3 d5 3. Bg5 c5 4. Bxf6 gxf6 5. e4 dxe4 6. d5

overview: White trades bishop for knight to ruin Black's pawns, then offers the d-pawn with e4 and d5 for space and development. Black can keep the e4 pawn but has doubled f-pawns and a lag in development; White follows with Qd2, O-O-O or Bb5+.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with d5 and develop Qd2, O-O-O
Pressure the weak Black pawns on f6 and h7

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn and support with ...Bg7 and ...Bd7

typical_structures.structure: Black has doubled f-pawns; White has a d5 pawn

character.notes: Unbalanced; White has a pawn deficit but Black has a damaged structure.

gambit.notes: After 5...dxe4 6.d5 Black is a pawn up and can keep it.

soundness.notes: Dubious for White; strong players prefer the main lines.

structure.notes: Semi-open: White d5 pawn and the open d- and e-files.

approach.notes: A sideline gambit rarely played at the top.

level.notes: Needs to know the specific lines.

character.reason: White gives a pawn for play against Black structure.

soundness.reason: Black can keep the pawn and the structure is not fatal.

structure.reason: The d5 pawn and d-file are open.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose the Malich.

plans.reason: White targets doubled pawns with space and development.
